lkw-fahrdynamik-01.question: Why does a fully loaded truck need a much longer braking distance than a car at the same speed?

options.a: Because trucks are generally fitted with weaker brakes than cars
options.b: Because kinetic energy increases with mass, so more energy must be dissipated to stop
options.c: Because truck tyres are made of softer rubber
options.d: Because truck drivers are legally required to react more slowly

lkw-fahrdynamik-01.explanation: A vehicle's kinetic energy rises in proportion to its mass. A heavily loaded truck must dissipate far more energy when braking than a car, which is why its stopping distance is significantly longer even with well-functioning brakes.

lkw-fahrdynamik-02.question: What two segments make up a truck's total stopping distance?

options.a: Sight distance and visibility distance
options.b: Pre-braking distance and post-braking distance
options.c: Reaction distance and braking distance
options.d: Steering distance and coasting distance

lkw-fahrdynamik-02.explanation: The stopping distance consists of the reaction distance (covered before the driver starts to brake) plus the actual braking distance (from applying the brakes to standstill). For heavy vehicles, the braking distance in particular is much longer than for cars.

lkw-fahrdynamik-03.question: Why are right turns by trucks especially prone to serious collisions with cyclists and pedestrians?

options.a: Because the area diagonally ahead and to the right of the cab is largely hidden from the driver's view
options.b: Because trucks are legally allowed to turn faster than cars
options.c: Because cyclists always have right of way over trucks when turning right
options.d: Because truck mirrors only show the area behind the vehicle

lkw-fahrdynamik-03.explanation: Because of the cab's height and seating position, a blind area forms right next to and slightly ahead of the driver, where cyclists and pedestrians are barely visible even with mirrors. These so-called turning accidents are among the most dangerous collision types in truck traffic — turning slowly and actively scanning the area is essential.

lkw-fahrdynamik-04.question: Which statement about a truck's blind spots (no-zones) is correct?

options.a: There is only one relevant blind spot, directly behind the vehicle
options.b: Modern mirror systems eliminate blind spots completely
options.c: Blind spots only exist when the vehicle is stationary, not while driving
options.d: There are several blind spots around a truck: in front, behind, and along both sides

lkw-fahrdynamik-04.explanation: Trucks typically have four blind-spot zones: directly in front of the cab, directly behind the vehicle, and along both the right and left sides. Other road users in these areas are barely or not at all visible to the driver, even with mirrors.

lkw-fahrdynamik-05.question: What does the term "swept path" (Schleppkurve) describe for a truck?

options.a: The maximum incline a truck can still climb
options.b: The path where the rear axle(s) track a tighter line than the front axle while cornering
options.c: The path a truck traces during an emergency stop
options.d: The distance a truck must maintain when overtaking

lkw-fahrdynamik-05.explanation: When turning, a truck's rear axle cuts the corner more tightly than the front axle (off-tracking). This means people or vehicles positioned on the inside of the curve can be struck by the rear of the vehicle or the trailer axle even after the cab has already passed.

lkw-fahrdynamik-06.question: Why does a truck often need more than one lane in a tight roundabout?

options.a: Because trucks generally have priority over all other vehicles in a roundabout
options.b: Because roundabout signage legally requires this for all vehicles over 3.5 t
options.c: Because the long wheelbase and the resulting swept path make it impossible to stay within a single lane
options.d: Because trucks are always required to reverse through roundabouts

lkw-fahrdynamik-06.explanation: Because of the long wheelbase and off-tracking, a truck often needs the full width of the roadway to get through a tight roundabout. Other road users should leave the truck enough room and avoid entering the roundabout alongside it.

lkw-fahrdynamik-07.question: Why do trucks face an increased risk of tipping over in tight curves or during sudden evasive maneuvers?

options.a: Because trucks generally have narrower tyres than cars
options.b: Because the high center of gravity creates a large tipping moment when cornering fast
options.c: Because truck steering systems respond more sluggishly than car steering
options.d: Because trucks do not come with power steering as standard

lkw-fahrdynamik-07.explanation: The higher a vehicle's center of gravity, the greater the tipping moment acting on the outer wheels during cornering or evasive maneuvers. For trucks with a tall body or high-mounted cargo, even a speed that would be harmless for a car can cause a rollover.

lkw-fahrdynamik-08.question: What function does an electronic stability program (ESP) perform in modern trucks?

options.a: It detects an impending skid or rollover and brakes individual wheels selectively to stabilize the vehicle
options.b: It automatically prevents any overloading of the vehicle
options.c: It removes the need to adjust speed for curves
options.d: It automatically controls the coupling when towing a trailer

lkw-fahrdynamik-08.explanation: ESP uses sensors to detect unstable driving states such as the onset of a skid or rollover, and stabilizes the vehicle through targeted braking of individual wheels and engine intervention. It significantly reduces rollover risk but does not replace driving at an appropriate speed.

lkw-fahrdynamik-09.question: Why is a partially filled tanker truck especially prone to tipping over during cornering or braking?

options.a: Because tank vehicles generally have a lower center of gravity than box-body trucks
options.b: Because liquids increase the braking effect of the axles
options.c: Because the liquid can slosh back and forth inside the tank, exerting sudden extra forces on the vehicle
options.d: Because tank vehicles are not allowed to be fitted with stability control

lkw-fahrdynamik-09.explanation: In a partially filled tank, liquid can start sloshing during steering or braking maneuvers. The resulting delayed, lateral forces can destabilize the vehicle and cause a rollover even at moderate cornering speeds.

lkw-fahrdynamik-10.question: Which vehicle is especially at risk of being pushed off course or tipping over in strong crosswinds?

options.a: A low, fully loaded tipper truck
options.b: An empty box body or curtainsider with a large side surface area
options.c: A vehicle with a particularly short wheelbase
options.d: A vehicle fitted with cruise control

lkw-fahrdynamik-10.explanation: Vehicles with a large, tall side surface — such as empty box bodies or curtainsiders — present a lot of surface area to the wind while weighing relatively little, so crosswind gusts, for example on bridges or forest clearings, can push the vehicle strongly off course or even cause it to tip over.

lkw-fahrdynamik-11.question: How should a truck driver behave to avoid collisions with low bridges or underpasses?

options.a: They can trust their instincts, since trucks generally fit under any bridge
options.b: They may rely solely on a standard car navigation device
options.c: Height restrictions only apply to vehicles towing a trailer
options.d: They should know the vehicle's actual height, check the route in advance, and consistently observe height-restriction signs

lkw-fahrdynamik-11.explanation: Truck drivers must know their vehicle's exact height, use appropriate truck-specific navigation, and take height-restriction signs seriously. Hitting a bridge that is too low can cause severe damage to the vehicle and infrastructure, as well as life-threatening accidents.

lkw-fahrdynamik-12.question: What must a truck driver pay particular attention to at a width restriction indicated by traffic signs?

options.a: The vehicle's actual overall width, including exterior mirrors and any load overhang
options.b: Only the width of the cab, since mirrors are not counted
options.c: Width restrictions apply exclusively to buses
options.d: They may ignore the restriction if no oncoming traffic is visible

lkw-fahrdynamik-12.explanation: The stated maximum width refers to the vehicle's total width, including exterior mirrors and any load protruding beyond the body. Ignoring this risks collisions with oncoming traffic, signs, or roadside furniture on narrow stretches of road.

lkw-fahrdynamik-13.question: Why can aquaplaning be dangerous for heavy commercial vehicles despite their higher axle loads?

options.a: Because heavy vehicles generally have less ground contact than cars
options.b: Because truck tyres are not allowed to have tread
options.c: Because at high speed a water film cannot be displaced quickly enough and the tyres can lose contact with the road surface, especially with worn tread
options.d: Because aquaplaning is legally excluded for vehicles over 3.5 t

lkw-fahrdynamik-13.explanation: A higher axle load does not automatically reduce the aquaplaning risk if speed, water depth, and tyre tread are unfavorable. At excessive speed, a wedge of water can form between the tyre and the road surface, causing the vehicle to lose contact with the road and become uncontrollable — speed must be adapted to weather and road conditions.

lkw-fahrdynamik-14.question: What minimum following distance must vehicles over 3.5 t gross weight maintain outside built-up areas when driving one behind another in the same lane at more than 50 km/h?

options.a: At least 20 metres
options.b: At least 50 metres
options.c: At least 100 metres
options.d: A distance left entirely to the driver's discretion

lkw-fahrdynamik-14.explanation: For vehicles over 3.5 t gross weight, a mandatory minimum gap of 50 metres to the vehicle ahead applies outside built-up areas at speeds above 50 km/h. This is meant to compensate for the longer braking distance caused by the vehicle's mass and to prevent rear-end collisions when driving in convoy.

lkw-fahrdynamik-15.question: To what maximum speed is the speed limiter on trucks over 3.5 t gross weight typically set?

options.a: 70 km/h
options.b: 90 km/h
options.c: 110 km/h
options.d: 130 km/h

lkw-fahrdynamik-15.explanation: Trucks over 3.5 t gross weight must be fitted with a speed limiter that technically caps the maximum speed at 90 km/h. This is intended to prevent excessive speeds, which would be especially risky given the vehicle's mass, braking distance, and rollover risk.

lkw-vorschriften-01.question: How often do trucks generally have to undergo a periodic roadworthiness inspection (Hauptuntersuchung)?

options.a: Every three years, as with new cars
options.b: Generally once a year
options.c: Only once mileage exceeds 100,000 km
options.d: Only once, at first registration

lkw-vorschriften-01.explanation: Because of their more intensive use and higher safety requirements, trucks and other commercial vehicles generally have to undergo a roadworthiness inspection once a year, much more often than newer cars.

lkw-vorschriften-02.question: What is the purpose of the additional safety inspection (SP) for trucks and trailers between periodic roadworthiness inspections?

options.a: To check safety-relevant components such as brakes, axles, and the coupling device in the interim
options.b: To measure only the engine's exhaust emissions
options.c: To document the quantity of cargo carried
options.d: It completely replaces the periodic roadworthiness inspection

lkw-vorschriften-02.explanation: The safety inspection is an additional, more frequent check specifically targeting safety-critical components such as the brake system, axles, tyres, and coupling device on commercial vehicles and trailers, in order to catch defects early between periodic roadworthiness inspections.

lkw-vorschriften-03.question: What is the purpose of axle-load scales used during truck inspections?

options.a: To measure engine power
options.b: To check tyre tread depth
options.c: To determine whether the permitted axle load or total gross weight has been exceeded
options.d: To determine the speed the vehicle was travelling at

lkw-vorschriften-03.explanation: Axle-load scales used at roadside checks measure the actual weight on each axle as well as the vehicle's total gross weight, making it possible to establish whether the permitted axle load or gross weight has been exceeded.

lkw-vorschriften-04.question: What consequences can significant overloading of a truck have?

options.a: None, as long as the load is properly secured
options.b: Only a minor warning with no further consequences
options.c: A shortened waiting period until the next roadworthiness inspection
options.d: A longer braking distance, increased rollover and tyre-damage risk, as well as fines up to a ban on continuing the journey

lkw-vorschriften-04.explanation: Overloading fundamentally changes handling: braking distance increases, rollover risk in curves rises, and tyres and axles can be overstressed. Depending on severity, roadside checks can result in substantial fines, penalty points, and in extreme cases a ban on continuing the journey until the load is reduced.

lkw-vorschriften-05.question: Who is responsible for ensuring a truck's cargo is properly secured?

options.a: Only the shipper of the goods
options.b: Primarily the driver, regardless of who originally loaded the vehicle
options.c: Only the haulage company as contracting party
options.d: No one, as long as the load looks fine from the outside

lkw-vorschriften-05.explanation: Even if other people were involved in loading the vehicle, the driver is responsible for checking that the cargo is safely secured before setting off. Inadequately secured cargo endangers driving stability and other road users.

lkw-vorschriften-06.question: What do orange warning plates on a truck generally indicate?

options.a: That the vehicle is towing a trailer over 750 kg
options.b: That the vehicle has a special permit for heavy-load transport
options.c: That dangerous goods are being transported, subject to special regulations
options.d: That the truck is used exclusively for long-distance haulage

lkw-vorschriften-06.explanation: Orange warning plates identify vehicles carrying dangerous goods. Such transports are subject to special dangerous-goods regulations (ADR) regarding labelling, equipment, driver qualification, and behaviour, since accidents involving these vehicles carry additional risks such as the release of hazardous substances.

lkw-vorschriften-07.question: Which vehicles are generally subject to Germany's Sunday and public-holiday driving ban?

options.a: All motor vehicles, regardless of permissible gross weight
options.b: Only vehicles towing a trailer over 750 kg
options.c: Trucks and truck combinations with a permissible gross weight over 7.5 t
options.d: Only vehicles transporting dangerous goods

lkw-vorschriften-07.explanation: Trucks and truck combinations with a permissible gross weight over 7.5 t are generally banned from road traffic between midnight and 10 pm on Sundays and public holidays. The aim is to relieve the road network and reduce noise on these days.

lkw-vorschriften-08.question: What type of transport is typically covered by an exception to the Sunday/holiday driving ban?

options.a: Transporting building materials for a private construction project
options.b: Transporting perishable food such as fresh milk
options.c: Transporting furniture for a private house move
options.d: Transporting construction vehicles to a new job site

lkw-vorschriften-08.explanation: Exceptions to the Sunday/holiday driving ban exist for transporting perishable goods such as fresh milk or other quickly-spoiling food, as well as for related empty runs, since a delay would render the goods unusable.

lkw-vorschriften-09.question: What generally must be observed when driving a truck into an environmental zone (Umweltzone)?

options.a: The truck generally needs the required emissions sticker corresponding to its emissions class
options.b: Environmental zones generally apply only to cars, not to trucks
options.c: A sticker is only required for trips over 100 km
options.d: Trucks are generally not allowed into environmental zones at all, regardless of the sticker

lkw-vorschriften-09.explanation: Environmental zones may generally only be entered by vehicles displaying the required emissions sticker for their pollutant class on the windscreen. This also applies to trucks; missing the required sticker can result in a fine.

lkw-vorschriften-10.question: What can police and the Federal Office for Goods Transport (BAG) check, among other things, during a truck inspection?

options.a: Only the vehicle's colour
options.b: Only the driver's personal clothing
options.c: Only the brand of the mounted tyres
options.d: Weight and load securing, the vehicle's technical condition, and driving/rest times using the tachograph

lkw-vorschriften-10.explanation: Roadside checks typically examine weight and axle load, load securing, the vehicle's technical condition (e.g. brakes, tyres), and driving/rest times recorded on the tachograph. Violations can result in fines and, in serious cases, a ban on continuing the journey.

lkw-vorschriften-11.question: Which documents must a professional truck driver generally be able to present during a roadside check?

options.a: Only their national ID card
options.b: Driving licence, vehicle registration documents, proof of driver qualification, and the records of driving and rest times
options.c: Only the freight documents, with no other proof required
options.d: No documents at all, if the journey takes place entirely within Germany

lkw-vorschriften-11.explanation: During checks, professional drivers must be able to present, among other things, a valid driving licence of the correct class, the vehicle's registration documents, proof of professional driver qualification, and the records of driving and rest times (e.g. tachograph data).

lkw-vorschriften-12.question: What absolutely must be checked before setting off with a coupled trailer?

options.a: Only the tyre pressure of the towing vehicle
options.b: Only whether the trailer is the correct colour
options.c: Whether the coupling is fully engaged and locked, confirmed by the locking indicator
options.d: The coupling check is only required for journeys over 100 km

lkw-vorschriften-12.explanation: Before any journey with a trailer, a visual check and the locking indicator must confirm that the coupling is fully engaged and secured. An incorrectly locked coupling can come loose while driving, causing the trailer to break away.

lkw-vorschriften-13.question: What is the purpose of the trailer's safety cable (breakaway cable)?

options.a: It serves solely to supply power to the lights
options.b: It automatically triggers the trailer's brakes if the coupling unintentionally separates
options.c: It keeps the trailer in its lane during normal cornering
options.d: It replaces the regular trailer coupling on short trips

lkw-vorschriften-13.explanation: If the trailer unintentionally detaches from the towing vehicle, the safety cable pulls a brake lever and thereby activates the trailer brake, bringing the detached trailer to as controlled a stop as possible. This safety device must be attached independently of the coupling itself.

lkw-vorschriften-14.question: Besides the mechanical coupling, which connections must also be made and checked when hitching a trailer?

options.a: Only the trailer coupling itself; on modern trailers no other connections are needed
options.b: Only the fuel line
options.c: Only the safety cable; electrical lines are optional
options.d: The electrical lines for the lighting and the compressed-air lines for the brake system, each followed by a function check

lkw-vorschriften-14.explanation: In addition to the mechanical coupling, the electrical lines for indicators, brake lights, and tail lights must be connected, along with the compressed-air lines for supply and brake pressure. Afterwards, the trailer's lighting and brakes must be checked to confirm they actually work before setting off.

lkw-vorschriften-15.question: How should a driver react if an articulated combination starts to jackknife during an emergency stop?

options.a: Ease off the brake in a controlled way, release the brake pedal, and correct steering as calmly and smoothly as possible
options.b: Press the brake even harder to stop the jackknifing
options.c: Countersteer as hard and quickly as possible to straighten the trailer
options.d: Manually release the coupling while driving

lkw-vorschriften-15.explanation: Jackknifing usually occurs when the wheels of the tractor unit or trailer lock up under braking and lateral grip is lost. Abrupt, hard countersteering or braking even harder typically makes the situation worse. The correct response is to ease off the braking force in a controlled way and steer smoothly so the wheels can regain stability.

lkw-ladungssicherung-01.question: Why can an unsecured pallet slide forward under emergency braking with a force far greater than its own weight?

options.a: Because the weight of the load actually increases while braking
options.b: Because during braking a deceleration force acts in addition to gravity, which depending on braking intensity can reach several times the load's weight
options.c: Because wooden pallets generally become lighter once they are in motion
options.d: Because the loading area tilts slightly forward during braking

lkw-ladungssicherung-01.explanation: During braking, an inertial force acts on the load in the direction of travel, depending on the deceleration achieved. In hard braking this force can be several times the load's weight. Unsecured load is therefore thrown forward, even though it sits perfectly still when the vehicle is stationary.

lkw-ladungssicherung-02.question: What is meant by form-fit (formschlüssig) load securing?

options.a: Securing the load solely through friction between the load and the loading surface
options.b: Attaching a warning sign to the load
options.c: Packing the load tightly against solid boundaries such as headboard, side walls or other cargo, so it has no room to move
options.d: Weighing the load before departure

lkw-ladungssicherung-02.explanation: Form-fit securing means the load is enclosed by fixed boundaries (walls, stanchions, other cargo) so there is virtually no gap left for it to shift. Together with force-fit securing (e.g. lashing straps), it is one of the two basic methods of load securing.

lkw-ladungssicherung-03.question: What is meant by force-fit (kraftschlüssig) load securing?

options.a: The load is pressed down onto the load bed with tie-down straps so firmly that the resulting friction force prevents it from sliding
options.b: The load is held solely by its own weight with no aids whatsoever
options.c: The load is form-fitted by clamping it between two side walls
options.d: The load is monitored using a GPS tracking system

lkw-ladungssicherung-03.explanation: In force-fit securing (tie-down lashing), the tension in the straps increases the pressure of the load onto the load bed. This raises the friction force that resists sliding. Its effectiveness strongly depends on the coefficient of friction between the load and the load bed.

lkw-ladungssicherung-04.question: What is the purpose of anti-slip mats in load securing?

options.a: They completely replace the need for tie-down straps
options.b: They reduce the weight of the load
options.c: They serve only to protect the load bed from scratches
options.d: They increase the coefficient of friction between the load and the load bed, improving the effect of force-fit securing

lkw-ladungssicherung-04.explanation: Anti-slip mats significantly increase the coefficient of friction between load and load bed. This achieves a stronger securing effect for the same lashing force. However, they do not replace additional securing by straps or form-fit measures, but complement them.

lkw-ladungssicherung-05.question: Under German law, who generally bears responsibility for adequate load securing?

options.a: Only the person who loaded the vehicle
options.b: Both the driver and the loader/keeper each have their own duties and can be held jointly responsible
options.c: Only the vehicle's registered keeper; the driver bears no responsibility at all
options.d: No one, because load securing is not legally regulated

lkw-ladungssicherung-05.explanation: The driver is obliged to check road safety, including load securing, before setting off. At the same time, the loader or keeper has their own duty of care when loading the vehicle. In the event of violations, several people can therefore be held responsible, depending on their respective contribution.

lkw-ladungssicherung-06.question: A driver takes over a truck that has already been loaded by a loading company. A check reveals the load was inadequately secured. Is the driver still responsible?

options.a: Yes, the driver is obliged to check the load securing before setting off and must not drive on if defects are recognisable
options.b: No, once a third party has loaded the vehicle, the driver is entirely free of any responsibility
options.c: No, the driver is only liable for technical defects on the vehicle, never for the load
options.d: Yes, but only if he personally helped with the physical loading

lkw-ladungssicherung-06.explanation: Even if a third party loaded the vehicle, the driver must check for recognisable securing defects before departure and must not drive off with a visibly unsafe load. The loader's responsibility does not release the driver from his own duty of care.

lkw-ladungssicherung-07.question: What consequences can arise during a roadside check if a load is inadequately secured but no concrete danger has yet occurred?

options.a: In principle there are no consequences at all as long as nothing has happened
options.b: Only a verbal warning with no legal effect
options.c: A warning fine or fine, and possibly an order that the journey may only continue once the load has been re-secured
options.d: Automatic revocation of the driving licence for at least one year

lkw-ladungssicherung-07.explanation: Even inadequate load securing without an actual incident can be sanctioned with a warning fine or fine. In addition, continuing the journey can be prohibited until the load has been properly secured.

lkw-ladungssicherung-08.question: What can result from inadequately secured load if it causes an accident?

options.a: Insurance always covers the full damage regardless of the cause
options.b: The driver and possibly the loader can face criminal and civil liability, and other road users can be seriously endangered or injured
options.c: There are no legal consequences as long as only the driver's own truck is damaged
options.d: Only the haulage company is liable; the driver is always uninvolved

lkw-ladungssicherung-08.explanation: Falling or shifting load can cause severe accidents with significant injury to other road users. Besides the danger to life and limb, the driver and loader face criminal and civil consequences, for example for negligent bodily harm or damages claims.

lkw-ladungssicherung-09.question: Why is correct distribution of the load across the load bed important for axle loads?

options.a: Because axle load has no influence at all on driving safety
options.b: Because only the total mass counts; distribution is legally irrelevant
options.c: Because uneven distribution can cause individual axle loads to be exceeded and impair steering, braking and driving stability
options.d: Because uneven distribution automatically reduces fuel consumption

lkw-ladungssicherung-09.explanation: Even if the permitted gross weight is maintained, unfavourable load distribution can overload individual axles. This impairs steerability, braking distance and driving stability, and can lead to technical damage as well as an increased risk of accidents.

lkw-ladungssicherung-10.question: How does a load's centre of gravity positioned too far to the rear typically affect a truck's handling?

options.a: It generally improves front-axle braking performance
options.b: It has no influence on handling whatsoever
options.c: It only improves comfort for the driver
options.d: It can reduce the load on the front axle and thereby worsen steering precision and lateral stability

lkw-ladungssicherung-10.explanation: If the load's centre of gravity sits too far towards the rear, the front axle is relieved of weight. This reduces steering precision and can decrease the lateral grip of the front tyres, which can become dangerous especially in curves and evasive manoeuvres.

lkw-ladungssicherung-11.question: Why does securing rolls, pipes or round material require particular care?

options.a: Because such loads are generally lighter than other goods
options.b: Because round cargo can easily roll away if there is no form-fit securing, which makes additional measures such as wedges or cradles necessary
options.c: Because round loads are not legally required to be secured
options.d: Because round material may only be transported on trailers

lkw-ladungssicherung-11.explanation: Cylindrical cargo such as pipes or coils tends to roll away under lateral forces or vibrations. Without wedges, cradles or other form-fit measures, the load can move uncontrollably even under relatively small forces.

lkw-ladungssicherung-12.question: What must be given particular attention when securing long loads such as steel beams or tree trunks?

options.a: Adequate securing against sliding both lengthwise and sideways as well as against tipping, since long cargo often extends across several stanchions or support points
options.b: Only the colour marking of the load
options.c: Ensuring the load rests as loosely as possible so it can shift if needed
options.d: The interior temperature of the driver's cab

lkw-ladungssicherung-12.explanation: Long loads such as beams or logs often rest on several support points and can both slide lengthwise and tip sideways. Careful securing must take both directions of movement into account, as well as possible bending of the material.

lkw-ladungssicherung-13.question: How should loose bulk material such as sand or gravel be transported on an open truck?

options.a: Without any special measures, since bulk material holds itself in place
options.b: Only on journeys of less than ten kilometres
options.c: With a suitable cover (e.g. a tarpaulin) to prevent material from falling off or being blown away during the journey
options.d: Only in open sacks with no further securing

lkw-ladungssicherung-13.explanation: Loose bulk material can fall off or be blown away by wind resistance, vibrations or braking, endangering other road users. A suitable cover prevents this and is mandatory for many types of bulk material.

lkw-ladungssicherung-14.question: What must be considered when stacking several crates or wire mesh boxes on top of each other?

options.a: It does not matter how the stacks are built as long as the total height is respected
options.b: Heavy, stable cargo should be placed at the bottom as far as possible, stack height must match the stability and load-bearing capacity of the lower layers, and the stack must additionally be secured against tipping
options.c: Light crates should generally be placed at the very bottom so they are not damaged during transport
options.d: Crates may only be transported in a single layer; stacking is generally not permitted

lkw-ladungssicherung-14.explanation: When stacking, the lower layer must be stable and strong enough to bear the weight of the layers above. In addition, the entire stack must be secured against sliding and tipping, since tall stacks are especially prone to tipping during cornering or braking.

lkw-ladungssicherung-15.question: What should a driver do if he notices during a break that the load has visibly shifted?

options.a: Stop the journey until the load has been properly re-secured or restowed, seeking assistance if necessary
options.b: Carefully continue to the destination at reduced speed, since a load that has already shifted generally does not move further
options.c: Just lock the side panels more firmly and continue without any further check
options.d: Ignore the observation if the schedule requires the journey to continue

lkw-ladungssicherung-15.explanation: A load that has already shifted shows that the original securing was inadequate. Continuing the journey carries a high risk that the load will move further or fall off. The journey may only continue once the load has been properly re-secured.

lkw-ladungssicherung-16.question: When should a driver check load securing during a longer journey?

options.a: Only at the very end of the journey, just before unloading
options.b: Never, since a single check before departure is legally sufficient
options.c: Before departure, again after a short distance, and then at regular intervals, especially after hard braking, evasive manoeuvres or uneven road surfaces
options.d: Only in the rain, since dry road surfaces have no influence on the load

lkw-ladungssicherung-16.explanation: Cargo can settle or shift even after a short distance, for example due to vibrations or an initial braking event. That is why load securing should be checked shortly after setting off and then at regular intervals, particularly after unusual driving situations.

lkw-ladungssicherung-17.question: How should a lashing strap be correctly tensioned in a tie-down application?

options.a: As loosely as possible, so the strap does not tear under vibration
options.b: With a suitable tensioning device (e.g. a ratchet), to the pre-tension force specified by the manufacturer or required for the load, without damaging the load or the strap
options.c: Only by hand, without any mechanical aid, to reliably rule out over-tensioning
options.d: At any tension level, since tension has no effect on the securing effect

lkw-ladungssicherung-17.explanation: The effectiveness of force-fit securing directly depends on the pre-tension achieved. A ratchet lashing strap must be tightened to a suitable tension to generate sufficient clamping pressure without damaging the load or overloading the strap.

lkw-ladungssicherung-18.question: Why is a single lashing strap laid centrally across a pallet often not enough to hold the load securely?

options.a: Because a single strap always tears immediately
options.b: Because a strap is legally approved only for loads under 50 kg
options.c: Because straps are generally used only for marking the load, not for securing it
options.d: Because a single strap often does not generate enough clamping pressure and does not reliably prevent sideways or lengthwise sliding, so several straps arranged appropriately are usually required

lkw-ladungssicherung-18.explanation: A single strap usually does not generate sufficiently even clamping pressure across the entire load area of the pallet and often does not adequately protect against sideways tipping or sliding. In practice, several straps at a suitable angle and spacing are therefore normally used.

lkw-ladungssicherung-19.question: What forces must adequate load securing on public roads generally cover?

options.a: Only forces that occur forward during acceleration
options.b: Forces that can act on the load forward during braking, sideways during cornering, and also vertically on uneven road surfaces
options.c: Only the force generated by crosswinds
options.d: Only static forces while the vehicle is stationary

lkw-ladungssicherung-19.explanation: Cargo must be secured so that it withstands the typical stresses of road traffic, including braking, cornering, evasive manoeuvres and uneven road surfaces. Securing that only accounts for one of these directions is generally inadequate.

lkw-ladungssicherung-20.question: Why is it important to know the coefficient of friction between the load and the load bed before calculating the required lashing force?

options.a: Because a lower coefficient of friction means more lashing force, or more or stronger lashing equipment, is needed to achieve the same securing effect
options.b: Because the coefficient of friction is only relevant for choosing the colour of the load bed
options.c: Because a high coefficient of friction generally makes any securing unnecessary
options.d: Because the coefficient of friction only matters on journeys abroad

lkw-ladungssicherung-20.explanation: The coefficient of friction determines how much holding force is available from friction alone. The smoother the surfaces, the lower the friction force, and the more additional securing through lashing equipment or anti-slip mats is needed to adequately secure the load.

lkw-ladungssicherung-21.question: Which combination of securing measures is often sensible in practical loading situations?

options.a: Only form-fit securing, since force-fit methods are legally prohibited
options.b: Only force-fit securing; form-fit measures are unnecessary
options.c: A combination of form-fit where possible (e.g. against the headboard or other cargo), supplemented by force-fit measures such as tie-down lashing for any remaining freedom of movement
options.d: It is sufficient to weigh the load once; no further measures are required

lkw-ladungssicherung-21.explanation: In practice, it is usually not possible to pack the entire load form-fit against solid boundaries. A combination of form-fit securing where possible, supplemented by force-fit securing with lashing straps, reliably covers any remaining freedom of movement.

lkw-ladungssicherung-22.question: What does the principle that a load must be 'stowed and secured' so that it 'cannot shift, fall over, fall off, or generate avoidable noise even under emergency braking or sudden evasive action' mean?

options.a: That the load only needs to be secured during calm, steady driving
options.b: That load securing must be designed to withstand unusual but foreseeable stresses that can occur in road traffic
options.c: That securing is only required for journeys above 80 km/h
options.d: That noise generated during the journey is legally completely irrelevant

lkw-ladungssicherung-22.explanation: This principle makes clear that load securing must not only be designed for normal conditions, but must also account for unusual yet realistic driving situations such as emergency braking or a sudden evasive manoeuvre.

lkw-ladungssicherung-23.question: Why should lashing straps be checked for damage such as cuts, abrasions or heavy wear before each use?

options.a: Because a damaged strap can tear under load and thereby suddenly and completely lose its securing effect
options.b: Because damaged straps are more visually conspicuous and therefore easier for inspectors to spot
options.c: Because new straps are generally less load-resistant than old, heavily worn straps
options.d: Because a visual inspection is legally required only for new vehicles

lkw-ladungssicherung-23.explanation: Damaged lashing straps lose part of their load capacity and can tear under sudden strain, for example during emergency braking. Regular visual inspection before use helps to identify and remove damaged straps in time.

lkw-ladungssicherung-24.question: A driver notices shortly before departure that the permitted lashing points on his vehicle are damaged. How should he act?

options.a: He should drive off anyway, since damaged lashing points only slightly impair load securing
options.b: He should additionally secure the load provisionally with adhesive tape and then set off
options.c: He should ignore the lashing points as long as the load looks stable on the load bed
options.d: He should not set off until intact lashing points are available or the load can be adequately secured by other means

lkw-ladungssicherung-24.explanation: Damaged lashing points can fail under load, endangering the entire securing chain. The driver bears responsibility for ensuring, before departure, that the load is adequately secured using intact and suitable equipment.

lkw-ladungssicherung-25.question: Why is it often not enough to rely solely on the load's own weight for heavy, compact single items (e.g. a machine)?

options.a: Because heavy loads may not be transported at all under any circumstances
options.b: Because the inertial forces acting during braking or cornering can shift even heavy items considerably if there is no adequate form-fit or sufficient lashing force
options.c: Because heavy loads must legally always be transported on a separate trailer
options.d: Because a load's own weight has no bearing on its stability during transport

lkw-ladungssicherung-25.explanation: Even heavy cargo can begin to move under strong deceleration or centrifugal forces if it is not additionally secured by form-fit or force-fit methods. The load's own weight does generate friction, but this is often insufficient to counteract all the forces that occur in road traffic.

lkw-ladungssicherung-26.question: What role does packaging (e.g. wrapping a pallet in stretch film) play in load securing?

options.a: Packaging completely replaces any form of technical load securing
options.b: Packaging has no influence at all on the load's stability
options.c: Stable packaging (e.g. tightly wrapped stretch film) can hold individual load units together and thereby support the effect of other securing measures, but does not fully replace them
options.d: Packaging serves only to protect against weather and has nothing to do with securing

lkw-ladungssicherung-26.explanation: Taut packaging can consolidate individual pieces into a more stable load unit and thereby reduce shifting of individual parts within that unit. However, it does not replace the necessary securing of the entire load unit against the load bed, for example through lashing straps or fixed boundaries.

lkw-ladungssicherung-27.question: What should a driver generally check regarding the load before departure?

options.a: Only the colour of the load, as this is decisive for road safety
options.b: Whether the permissible gross weight and axle loads are respected, and whether the load is properly distributed and secured against sliding, tipping and falling off
options.c: Only the fuel level; the load itself is checked by the loading staff and is none of the driver's business
options.d: Whether the load carries enough promotional stickers

lkw-ladungssicherung-27.explanation: Checking load securing before departure is one of the driver's fundamental duties. This includes complying with the permitted weights, ensuring suitable load distribution, and providing effective securing against sliding, tipping or falling off.

lkw-ladungssicherung-28.question: Why can even a relatively small object falling from a moving truck be very dangerous for following road users?

options.a: Because a falling object carries considerable impact energy at high driving speed and represents a sudden, barely predictable obstacle for following vehicles, especially motorcyclists or car occupants
options.b: Because small objects can never cause any damage
options.c: Because by law falling objects automatically come to rest and cannot roll away
options.d: Because following vehicles are legally required to maintain a distance of at least 200 metres

lkw-ladungssicherung-28.explanation: Even smaller objects can carry considerable kinetic energy at high speed and constitute a sudden obstacle for following vehicles. This can be especially dangerous for riders of two-wheelers, as evasive action is often only possible to a limited extent.

lkw-ladungssicherung-29.question: Why is careful planning of the loading sequence sensible for mixed cargo with packages of different weights and sizes?

options.a: Because the loading sequence only matters for loading time, not for safety
options.b: Because light goods must always be stacked at the bottom and heavy goods on top
options.c: Because a well-thought-out arrangement helps to avoid gaps, keep the centre of gravity favourable, and enables form-fit securing between the individual packages
options.d: Because mixed cargo is generally prohibited by law

lkw-ladungssicherung-29.explanation: A well-planned loading sequence reduces gaps in which cargo could shift and makes it possible to place heavy items as low and central as possible. This helps to keep the centre of gravity favourable and improves form-fit securing between the individual packages.

lkw-ladungssicherung-30.question: What is the most important basic rule if a driver is unsure whether the load is adequately secured?

options.a: He should simply set off and monitor the situation while driving
options.b: When in doubt, he should take further securing measures or seek expert assistance before setting off, since safety always takes precedence over time pressure
options.c: He should ignore the doubt as long as the load looks tidy from the outside
options.d: He should leave the decision entirely to the following traffic

lkw-ladungssicherung-30.explanation: When in doubt about load securing, the principle applies that safety takes precedence over saving time. If there is any doubt about whether the load is adequately secured, the driver should take additional measures or seek expert help rather than accept an avoidable risk.

lkw-lenkzeiten-01.question: What is the main purpose of the legal driving and rest time rules for professional drivers?

options.a: To reduce transport costs for haulage companies.
options.b: To prevent driver fatigue at the wheel and thereby increase road safety.
options.c: Solely to extend engine service life.
options.d: They exclusively regulate the loading of commercial vehicles.

lkw-lenkzeiten-01.explanation: Fatigue is a major cause of accidents in commercial road transport. Driving and rest time rules ensure drivers are sufficiently rested to participate safely in traffic.

lkw-lenkzeiten-02.question: What is the normal maximum daily driving time for a professional driver?

options.a: 6 hours
options.b: 12 hours
options.c: 9 hours, which may be extended on up to two days per week
options.d: 15 hours without any restriction

lkw-lenkzeiten-02.explanation: The daily driving time is generally limited to 9 hours, extendable to up to 10 hours on a maximum of two days per week.

lkw-lenkzeiten-03.question: After what maximum period of continuous driving must a driver take a break?

options.a: After 4.5 hours
options.b: After 8 hours
options.c: After 2 hours
options.d: After 6.5 hours

lkw-lenkzeiten-03.explanation: After a maximum of 4.5 hours of driving, a break of at least 45 minutes must be taken, unless a rest period begins instead.

lkw-lenkzeiten-04.question: How may the required 45-minute driving break be split?

options.a: Freely into several 5-minute segments
options.b: Only as a single uninterrupted 45-minute break; splitting is never allowed
options.c: Into two segments of 22.5 minutes each
options.d: Into a first segment of at least 15 minutes followed by a second of at least 30 minutes, in that order

lkw-lenkzeiten-04.explanation: The break can be split: first at least 15 minutes, then at least 30 minutes, together at least 45 minutes within the 4.5-hour driving period.

lkw-lenkzeiten-05.question: What is the minimum length of a professional driver's regular daily rest period?

options.a: 6 hours
options.b: 11 hours
options.c: 24 hours
options.d: 3 hours

lkw-lenkzeiten-05.explanation: The regular daily rest period must be at least 11 consecutive hours. It may be reduced on certain days.

lkw-lenkzeiten-06.question: To how many hours may the daily rest period be reduced as a so-called reduced daily rest period?

options.a: To 5 hours
options.b: To 11 hours, i.e. not at all
options.c: To at least 9 hours, but only on a limited number of days between two weekly rest periods
options.d: To 2 hours, as often as desired

lkw-lenkzeiten-06.explanation: The daily rest period may be reduced to at least 9 hours, but only on a limited number of days between two weekly rest periods.

lkw-lenkzeiten-07.question: What is meant by the weekly rest period under the driving and rest time rules?

options.a: A continuous rest period the driver must take once a week in addition to the daily rest periods
options.b: The sum of all lunch breaks in a working week
options.c: A voluntary rest period with no legal regulation
options.d: The time the driver spends washing the vehicle

lkw-lenkzeiten-07.explanation: In addition to daily rest periods, the driver must regularly take a longer, continuous weekly rest period, which serves recovery after several working days.

lkw-lenkzeiten-08.question: How is the maximum weekly driving time generally limited?

options.a: There is no weekly limit, only a daily one
options.b: To 56 hours per week, with an additional limit over two consecutive weeks
options.c: To 20 hours per week
options.d: To 100 hours per week

lkw-lenkzeiten-08.explanation: Driving time within one week must not exceed 56 hours; an additional limit applies over two consecutive weeks to prevent sustained overload.

lkw-lenkzeiten-09.question: What is the function of the tachograph in a truck?

options.a: It only measures the engine's fuel consumption
options.b: It is only used for navigation and route planning
options.c: It records the driver's driving time, breaks, rest periods, and other activities
options.d: It exclusively monitors tire pressure

lkw-lenkzeiten-09.explanation: The tachograph automatically documents the driver's various activities, enabling checks on compliance with driving and rest time rules.

lkw-lenkzeiten-10.question: Which categories of activity does a tachograph typically distinguish?

options.a: Driving time, availability time, other work, and rest/break time
options.b: Only driving time and engine standstill
options.c: Only the distance travelled in kilometers
options.d: Only the outside temperature during the journey

lkw-lenkzeiten-10.explanation: The tachograph distinguishes between driving time, availability time, other work, and rest time or breaks, so that compliance with legal requirements can be verified.

lkw-lenkzeiten-11.question: What is the driver card used with a digital tachograph?

options.a: A credit card for paying tolls
options.b: A replacement for the driving licence with no other function
options.c: A vehicle diagnostic tool unrelated to driving times
options.d: A personal chip card on which that driver's individual activities are stored

lkw-lenkzeiten-11.explanation: The driver card is personal and stores that individual driver's driving, work and rest times over an extended period.

lkw-lenkzeiten-12.question: What is the fundamental difference between the older analog tachograph and the digital tachograph?

options.a: The analog tachograph requires no recording of driver activity at all
options.b: The analog tachograph records data on a circular paper chart disc, while the digital tachograph stores data electronically on a driver card and mass memory
options.c: The digital tachograph can only be installed in passenger cars
options.d: There is no difference; both systems work identically

lkw-lenkzeiten-12.explanation: Analog systems use a circular paper chart for mechanical recording, while digital systems store data electronically and encrypted on the driver card and the vehicle's mass memory.

lkw-lenkzeiten-13.question: What consequences can tampering with a tachograph have for the driver and the company?

options.a: Substantial fines, criminal prosecution, and loss of the reliability required for professional driving
options.b: No consequences at all, since the tachograph is merely a recommendation
options.c: Only a warning with no further consequences
options.d: Only a delay of the vehicle's next roadworthiness inspection

lkw-lenkzeiten-13.explanation: Tampering with a tachograph is a serious regulatory offence or criminal act and can lead to heavy fines, criminal proceedings, and the withdrawal of the reliability status required of drivers and operators.

lkw-lenkzeiten-14.question: What particular danger arises from exceeding the permitted driving times?

options.a: A slightly higher fuel bill
options.b: An increased risk of accidents due to the fatigued driver's declining attention, reaction ability, and concentration
options.c: Faster wear of the vehicle's tires
options.d: A shortened service life of the tachograph

lkw-lenkzeiten-14.explanation: Fatigue significantly impairs reaction ability and concentration and is one of the most common causes of serious truck accidents. This is precisely why driving time limits exist.

lkw-lenkzeiten-15.question: Who is responsible for ensuring a driver keeps proper tachograph records?

options.a: Only the vehicle registration authority
options.b: No one; recording happens automatically with no responsibility on the driver
options.c: Both the driver and the company each have their own duties regarding proper use and retention of the records
options.d: Only the vehicle manufacturer

lkw-lenkzeiten-15.explanation: Both the driver (correct operation, carrying required records) and the company (organisation, data backup, oversight) have their own independent duties relating to the tachograph.

lkw-lenkzeiten-16.question: What should a driver do if, for example due to a traffic jam or an urgent customer appointment, they would have to exceed their permitted driving time?

options.a: Exceed the driving time without restriction, since external circumstances justify any overrun
options.b: Manually switch the tachograph to rest mode while still driving to conceal the overrun
options.c: Switch off the recording so the overrun is not documented
options.d: Plan a suitable break or rest period in good time and, if in doubt, interrupt the journey rather than exceed the permitted driving time

lkw-lenkzeiten-16.explanation: Time pressure does not justify exceeding driving times. The driver must plan ahead and, if in doubt, interrupt the journey to comply with the rules and maintain safety.

lkw-lenkzeiten-17.question: What is recorded under the tachograph activity category "availability time"?

options.a: Periods when the driver does not have to work but must remain available, e.g. while a co-driver is driving or while waiting for loading/unloading
options.b: Only the pure time spent actively driving
options.c: The time spent on private shopping during a rest period
options.d: Only the time of the vehicle's annual roadworthiness inspection

lkw-lenkzeiten-17.explanation: Availability time covers waiting periods in which the driver must remain available without actively working, such as during loading or unloading by third parties or while riding as a co-driver in a moving vehicle.

lkw-lenkzeiten-18.question: What does the Sunday and public-holiday driving ban for trucks over 7.5 tonnes in Germany fundamentally state?

options.a: It bans all truck journeys on every day of the week
options.b: It only applies to vehicles under 3.5 tonnes
options.c: On Sundays and certain public holidays, trucks with a permissible gross weight over 7.5 tonnes generally may not use public roads
options.d: It only concerns journeys within built-up areas

lkw-lenkzeiten-18.explanation: The Sunday and public-holiday driving ban generally prohibits trucks with a permissible gross weight over 7.5 tonnes from using public roads on Sundays and certain public holidays, in order to reduce traffic burden.

lkw-lenkzeiten-19.question: Which of the following types of cargo is a typical example of an exception to the Sunday and public-holiday driving ban?

options.a: Construction materials for a building site starting on Monday
options.b: Highly perishable food such as fresh fruit or fresh milk
options.c: Furniture for a private house move
options.d: Building materials for a construction project with no particular urgency

lkw-lenkzeiten-19.explanation: Recognised exceptions to the Sunday and public-holiday driving ban exist for highly perishable goods such as fresh fruit, vegetables or milk, since a delay would cause the goods to spoil.

lkw-lenkzeiten-20.question: What generally applies when two drivers take turns driving the same vehicle (multi-manning)?

options.a: Each driver must still have their individual driving, availability, and rest times correctly recorded via their own driver card
options.b: Only one of the two drivers needs a driver card; the times are combined
options.c: Driving time rules no longer apply at all once two drivers are used
options.d: The second driver may remain in the vehicle indefinitely without any rest period

lkw-lenkzeiten-20.explanation: Even in multi-manning operation, driving and rest time rules apply individually to each driver; each driver needs their own driver card and must observe their own rest periods.

lkw-lenkzeiten-21.question: What falls under the tachograph category "other work"?

options.a: Only the time spent behind the wheel while driving
options.b: Only the daily rest period taken in the vehicle
options.c: Activities such as loading and unloading, cleaning, technical maintenance, or administrative tasks connected with the transport
options.d: Only the driver's private errands

lkw-lenkzeiten-21.explanation: Other work covers activities besides driving that are connected with the driver's occupation, such as loading and unloading, vehicle upkeep, or administrative tasks.

lkw-lenkzeiten-22.question: What must a driver do if their driver card is lost or damaged in the short term?

options.a: They may never drive a truck again for the rest of their career
options.b: They must continue the journey immediately with no further documentation at all
options.c: There is no reporting obligation whatsoever; the loss can be ignored
options.d: They must report the loss or damage, produce a printout where required, and manually document the journey according to applicable rules until a replacement card is issued

lkw-lenkzeiten-22.explanation: In case of loss or damage of the driver card, reporting and documentation obligations apply so that driving and rest times remain traceable until a replacement card is issued.

lkw-lenkzeiten-23.question: Why must tachograph data be retained for a certain period and downloaded regularly?

options.a: So that enforcement authorities and the company can retrospectively verify compliance with driving and rest time rules
options.b: Because otherwise the data would automatically reduce engine power
options.c: Solely to calculate fuel consumption
options.d: Only to create photographs of the route travelled

lkw-lenkzeiten-23.explanation: Retaining and regularly downloading the data allows authorities and companies to check compliance retrospectively and detect violations.

lkw-lenkzeiten-24.question: What must fundamentally be true of a rest period for it to count as a rest period under the rules?

options.a: It may be interrupted at any time by brief driving activity without any consequence
options.b: It must be uninterrupted, and the driver must be able to use it freely without having to work
options.c: It must necessarily be spent outside the vehicle
options.d: It only counts if it lasts longer than 24 hours

lkw-lenkzeiten-24.explanation: A rest period must be uninterrupted and must allow the driver to freely dispose of that time, free from any work obligations.

lkw-lenkzeiten-25.question: What generally applies when a driver spends part of a rest period on a ferry or train?

options.a: Such a rest period is never permitted under any circumstances and must always be discarded
options.b: The rest period automatically counts double
options.c: Under certain conditions the rest period can be credited while on a ferry or train, provided the driver has access to a suitable sleeper cabin or berth
options.d: Time spent on the ferry always counts as full driving time

lkw-lenkzeiten-25.explanation: Under certain conditions, such as access to a sleeper cabin, a rest period taken during a ferry or train crossing can be credited, reflecting rules designed for combined transport.

lkw-lenkzeiten-26.question: What role does the company (employer) play in ensuring drivers comply with driving and rest time rules?

options.a: The company bears no responsibility at all; only the driver is liable for everything
options.b: The company must organise the work so that the driver can comply with the rules, and is obliged to check the records
options.c: The company may instruct the driver to exceed driving times whenever operationally necessary
options.d: The company is only responsible for maintaining the tachograph, not for scheduling

lkw-lenkzeiten-26.explanation: The company is obliged to design work processes and schedules so that driving and rest times can be complied with, and must regularly check the records.

lkw-lenkzeiten-27.question: What generally happens if a driver takes a reduced weekly rest period?

options.a: The reduction must be compensated within a certain period by an equivalent rest period taken together with another rest period
options.b: A reduced weekly rest period never needs to be compensated and has no further consequences
options.c: The driver automatically loses their driving licence as a result
options.d: A reduction of the weekly rest period is never permitted under any circumstances

lkw-lenkzeiten-27.explanation: A reduced weekly rest period must be compensated by a corresponding period of compensatory rest attached to another rest period, in order to ensure overall recovery.

lkw-lenkzeiten-28.question: What do enforcement authorities typically check during a roadside inspection regarding driving and rest times?

options.a: Only the cleanliness of the driver's cab
options.b: Only the load-securing plan
options.c: The tachograph records of recent days, signs of tampering, and the driver's current activity
options.d: Only the validity of the driving licence

lkw-lenkzeiten-28.explanation: Roadside inspections routinely check tachograph data from recent days and possible signs of tampering, in order to detect violations of driving and rest time rules.

lkw-lenkzeiten-29.question: How often may the daily driving time be extended to 10 hours within a two-week period?

options.a: As often as desired, with no restriction
options.b: Only once every two weeks
options.c: Never; such an extension is never permitted
options.d: On a maximum of two days per week, i.e. limited overall within each week

lkw-lenkzeiten-29.explanation: Extending the daily driving time to up to 10 hours is limited to a maximum of two days per week, in order to prevent sustained overload.

lkw-lenkzeiten-30.question: Why is it useful for a professional driver to know the basics of driving and rest time rules even without relying solely on the tachograph display?

options.a: Because the tachograph is checked only once every ten years anyway
options.b: Because the driver must be able to independently plan the journey and breaks and correctly judge in everyday practice when a break or rest period is required
options.c: Because the rules only apply to journeys abroad anyway
options.d: Because it extends the vehicle's maintenance intervals

lkw-lenkzeiten-30.explanation: Even though the tachograph monitors compliance, the driver must understand the rules to independently and proactively plan journeys and breaks, avoiding violations in the first place.
